title: Measuring Teamwork Attitudes in Nursing Students: Psychometric Evaluation of the Croatian T-TAQ and Changes During an Undergraduate Elective Course
content: Background: Effective teamwork is essential for safe nursing care, and positive attitudes toward teamwork should be developed during nursing education. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the TeamSTEPPS® Teamwork Attitudes Questionnaire (T-TAQ) for Croatian nursing students, evaluate its measurement properties, and examine changes in teamwork attitudes during an undergraduate elective course informed by TeamSTEPPS® principles. Methods: A cross-sectional psychometric evaluation (n = 446) was combined with a single-group pre–post assessment of first-year students (n = 51 matched pairs). Measurement properties were evaluated according to the COSMIN framework. Results: Overall internal consistency was high (Cronbach’s α = 0.953); subscale coefficients ranged from 0.623 to 0.950, with Mutual Support showing the lowest value. The initial five-factor model had inadequate absolute fit, which improved after post hoc correlated residuals were specified among negatively worded items (CFI = 0.999; TLI = 0.999; scaled RMSEA = 0.059). Overall teamwork attitude scores increased significantly after the course (Z = −3.639, p < 0.001, r = 0.36), with improvements in Team Structure, Situation Monitoring, Communication, and Leadership, but not in Mutual Support. Conclusions: The Croatian T-TAQ showed high overall internal consistency, but its factor structure and domain-level reliability require further validation. Students’ teamwork attitudes improved after the course, although these changes cannot be attributed directly to it.
